look_here_first: Cream-white ELONGATED flower SPIKES (rather than round heads of S. roemeriana), distinctive hooked prickles on woody twigs and notably broader/longer leaflets than most Gregg's catclaw. For Gregg versus Wright, measure several mature leaflets and check whether the inflorescence is comparatively loose and whether ripe pods curl.

morphology_keys.habit: Thorny shrub or small tree, locally sometimes tree-sized.
morphology_keys.armature: Short hooked recurved internodal prickles on stems, not paired stipular spines.
morphology_keys.leaves: Bipinnate, often 1–4 pairs of pinnae and 3–6 paired obovate leaflets per pinna; literature reports variable leaflet dimensions. Compare same-maturity leaves against Gregg's catclaw.
morphology_keys.flowers: Cream to yellowish-white flower SPIKES, elongated rather than spherical, often more open/less compact than Gregg's.
morphology_keys.pods: Broad, flat pods, often slightly constricted; can be distorted or coiled, so curvature alone not definitive.
best_field_traits: Larger round-obovate leaflets than typical Gregg's catclaw

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. roemeriana has rounded white flower heads; S. greggii and S. wrightii have spikes. Relative leaflet size and density of flowering spike provide best Gregg/Wright field hints; use fruit and reproductive context for difficult cases. Texas A&M gives Wright leaflet length 0.25–0.5 in vs Gregg less than 0.25 in; 2024 publication gives partially overlapping shorter ranges, so don't apply one absolute cutoff.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew Texas native at state scale and Texas A&M Uvalde habitat; no 3 counties certified in target-zone; none invented.

diagnostic_image_needs: whole flower spike with several paired leaflets
complete bipinnate leaf with millimeter scale
mature pod with stalk and ruler
same-scale leaflet and pod side-by-side against Gregg
